adversarial_audit.objection: The earlier O(n^-2) average permits polynomial filtering.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Summing reciprocal class sizes before bounding them sharpens the average to at most 7/(4p(n)).

adversarial_audit.objection: A soft filter can beat hard threshold postselection.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The moment-budget inequality holds for every fractional weight in [0,1]; exact finite linear programs audit this.

adversarial_audit.objection: Polynomially many source labels repair the rarity.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The maximum-score expectation gains only the union factor K, which cannot overcome p(n)=2^Omega(sqrt(n)).

adversarial_audit.objection: Every coherent collective strategy is a central filter.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No. The theorem does not cover interference that builds a new multi-sector statistic without accepting one high-score label.

claim_gate.reason: Any label-diagonal route to inverse-polynomial commutator signal has stretched-exponentially small success, even after polynomial source multiplicity; a viable route must create a new collective observable on typical sectors.

falsifiers_triggered: The O(n^-2) class-size bound was far too weak for filter accounting.
Soft central weights do not evade the unnormalized moment budget.
Generic amplitude amplification cannot remove a partition-number cost.
The theorem does not justify rejecting new collective observables.

proof_obligations.resolution: Moved-support decomposition, exact m<=22 controls, and the partition/centralizer/factorial tail prove the 7/4 bound.
Since 0<=w<=1, accepted unnormalized score is at most the source expectation; division by success gives the tradeoff.
The normalized character ratio lies in [-1,1], giving pointwise domination factor kappa=2.
The subset injection proves p(n)>=2^Omega(sqrt(n)); the square root of the reciprocal acceptance is still superpolynomial.
A coherent transform may combine typical sectors into a new observable rather than selecting a high-A source label.

summary: Closed central postselection onto rare commutator-sensitive sectors; only genuinely collective typical-sector interference remains open.

theorem.architecture_scope: Public label-diagonal central filters selecting one high-moment source sector; new collective observables are outside scope.
theorem.asymptotic_consequence: Polynomial K,kappa,1/tau imply exp(-Omega(sqrt(n))) acceptance; generic amplitude amplification costs exp(Omega(sqrt(n))).
